newsitem.title: UK: UK's Sainsbury's uses ferry for supplies.
newsitem.headline: UK's Sainsbury's uses ferry for supplies.

text.p: British retail chain owner Sainsbury's said on Friday that it had chartered its own ferry to collect fresh produce from northern Spain to beat the French lorry drivers' dispute and deliver supplies to its 371 supermarkets.
The first ferry set sail on Friday from Harwich for Santander, in northern Spain where it would arrive on December 2, 1996.
The ship would re-embark on the same day carrying fruits and vegetables and return to Harwich on December 4, 1996.

Meanwhile, French truckers were moving towards ending their dispute late on Friday after their unions signed a deal with employers on early retirement and reported substantial progress on pay and work-time claims.
Friday was the twelfth day of the truckers' strike.
